name: Icon
summary: A glyph of the system's icon set, decorative or named.
description: An icon draws one glyph of the icon set (Material Symbols, the Iconography foundation) at a size and in a color of the system. Next to text it is decoration and says nothing to assistive technology; alone, it must be named by what it means, and is then exposed as an image. Icons inside the other components (buttons, alerts, selects) are those components' parts, styled by their tokens; this component is for icons placed by a product in its own content.

anatomy.description: Root: the glyph itself, hidden or exposed as an image named by its label. Carries the size and the color.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Side of the square the glyph fills.

properties.name: Color
properties.description: Color of the glyph: the surrounding text color, or one of the system's icon roles.

options.description: Inherits the color of the text around it. The default.
The secondary icon color: quieter than the text.

properties.name: Glyph
properties.description: Name of the glyph in the icon set (its Material Symbols name).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the icon means, when it stands alone (Warning, Verified account). Without it the icon is decorative and hidden.

states.description: The only state: an icon has no interaction.

notes: A square of the size, aligned on the middle of the surrounding text.
An icon never stretches; the glyph fills the square as the icon font draws it.

name.text: Without a label the icon is decoration, hidden from assistive technology. With a label it is an image named by that label (role img and aria-label on the web): the label says what the icon means, not what it looks like.

guidelines.text: An icon next to text that says the same thing is pure decoration: it is implemented so assistive technology ignores it, and the text carries the structure. An icon that stands for something by itself has a text alternative naming its meaning.
Render the glyph as its ligature name in a span: with aria-hidden="true" when decorative (the ligature name would otherwise be read as text), with role="img" and aria-label when named.

A named icon is a graphical object required to understand the content: it contrasts at least 3:1 with the surface in every color mode. On the default surface the system's icon roles give 12.87:1 (neutral, light) and 8.80:1 (dark), 5.79:1 and 12.80:1 (brand), 7.87:1 and 6.08:1 (success), 4.52:1 and 4.97:1 (error), 4.96:1 and 8.58:1 (info); the warning icon color is 13.01:1 in light mode but 2.14:1 in dark mode, a Figma library limit. A decorative icon has no contrast requirement.
The color of an icon never carries its meaning alone: a status icon is paired with text or named by its label.
Provide alternative text labels for custom interface icons; they let VoiceOver describe what is on screen.
Pass null as the contentDescription of a decorative icon; describe a meaningful one by its purpose.

guidelines: The label of a named icon says its meaning, as a noun or a short phrase: Warning, Verified, Locked; never the glyph's name.
Use the same glyph for the same meaning everywhere in a product.

examples.name: Medium, brand, named
examples.description: Stands alone: exposed as an image named by its label.

decisions.text: An icon is a glyph of the icon font (Iconography foundation: Material Symbols Outlined, fill off, weight 300, grade 0, optical size 20) at 16, 20 or 24 px (small, medium, large).

By default an icon inherits the surrounding text color (no token: currentColor); the other options read the Figma library's on-base icon roles: neutral (secondary), brand, success, warning, error, info.
An icon is decorative and hidden unless it is given a label, which then names it as an image.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions icon-font-glyph, colors, decorative-unless-named). A span holding one glyph, hidden or named; sizes small, medium, large; seven colors. Named icon contrast on the default surface, light / dark: neutral 12.87 / 8.80, brand 5.79 / 12.80, success 7.87 / 6.08, warning 13.01 / 2.14, error 4.52 / 4.97, info 4.96 / 8.58.
